title: Legal Effect is a source-grounded effect domain, not an LLM opinion
summary: The legal pipeline separates what a source says, what a proposed interpretation claims, what has survived structured interrogation/challenge, what the Legal Effect compiler has certified, and what Institutional Policy has published. A model may propose or explain; it does not create legal authority.
invariants: An assertion in a contract, demand letter, statute, model response or commentary is not automatically an operative Legal Effect.
Original source material and exact source/provision identity remain traceable through the derived proposition and effect.
Legal Effect constrains the feasible action space; it does not choose the business optimum.
Unknown, contested or semantically unresolved meaning remains explicit and can require legal review rather than being guessed.
Institutional Policy publication and Legal Effect semantics are separate authority boundaries.

provenance.claim: Legal Effect v0.14 owns structured legal-effect evaluation and the compiler/certification authority boundary; public legal API remains legal.effect/0.10.
Institutional Policy owns fixed/versioned publication identity, authority, effective time, lifecycle, topology, rollout and replay rather than domain legal semantics.
Legal Interrogation dev5 implements clause interrogation, proposition challenge, lifecycle invalidation and a real Intention Service dev11 discovery adapter.
